title: The homepage's one primary CTA dumps visitors onto a 100%-client-rendered mega-page that paints empty
evidence: src/app/mission-control/page.tsx:1 ('use client' on the entire page component); src/app/mission-control/loading.tsx (skeleton with 'Loading live data...'); LandingHero.tsx:227-248 (single primary CTA 'See every upcoming launch' -> /mission-control); curl of the live URL returns a shell containing only one literal 'Loading' occurrence, no server-rendered launch content
experience: A first-time visitor's only above-the-fold action is one big CTA that says 'See every upcoming launch.' They click it, and instead of a countdown or a launch list they get a generic pulsing skeleton while ~20 client modules import and the page fetches its data client-side. On a phone on real-world mobile data this is several seconds of nothing before the thing they clicked for (a rocket) appears.
recommendation: Server-render (or statically pre-render with ISR) at least the next-launch hero block of Mission Control - countdown, mission name, watch-live button - so the CTA's destination has real content in the initial HTML instead of a skeleton.
why: Verified src/app/mission-control/page.tsx:1 has 'use client' on the whole page (30 imports, no server component). Live curl of the 94KB response contains exactly one 'Loading live data...' string and zero occurrences of real launch content, confirming the initial HTML ships the skeleton.

title: Exit-intent popup fires on an ordinary mobile scroll gesture and leads with a paid trial, not the free newsletter
evidence: src/components/marketing/ExitIntentPopup.tsx:99-118 (mobile trigger: any scroll past 500px followed by a fast scroll back above 50px, after 15s on page) and :26,251-259 (defaults to the 'Free 14-Day Trial' tab, 'Limited time offer' copy, ahead of the 'Free Weekly Brief' tab); mounted globally in src/app/layout.tsx:32,338
experience: Scrolling down a viewing guide and then flicking back to the top to tap a nav link - normal behavior, not an exit signal - triggers a full-screen 'Wait - before you go' modal defaulting to a Pro-trial pitch with an urgency line. It interrupts the enthusiast flow and leads with the paid tier before the free option.
recommendation: Drop the fast-scroll-to-top mobile heuristic or gate it behind a real proxy like tab-blur/back-button; default the modal to the free newsletter tab, keeping Pro secondary.
why: Trigger logic is maxScroll>500 && currentY<50 && previous-sample>200 with no debounce. useState('trial') confirms the trial default. Mounted globally in layout.tsx via next/dynamic.

title: The first dropdown a rocket fan opens ('Launches') has 18 items with no 'start here'
evidence: src/lib/site-directory.ts:41-62 lists ~20 entries in the launches group
experience: Someone who 'likes rockets' opens the menu closest to their intent and is handed undifferentiated choices with non-obvious names.
recommendation: Visually separate a 3-item 'Start here' group from the long tail of specialist tools.
why: Navigation.tsx:41-48 filters to nav:true entries only - 8 items + 'Everything in Launches', not 18. The 2026-08-28 nav overhaul already fixed the overload. Residual: the `hot` flag exists in the data model but Navigation.tsx's DropdownItem type drops it, so the rendered 9-item list still has no visual 'start here' grouping.

title: 'Launches by Site' shows a wall of 16 spaceport cards, not the launches themselves
evidence: src/app/launches/page.tsx:27-33 - the only content is an h1 and a map over `sites` rendering one card per spaceport; no chronological list of upcoming launches
experience: A visitor expecting to see what's flying next lands on 16 near-identical spaceport cards and has to pick a site blind before seeing any actual launch.
recommendation: Put a compact 'next 5 launches across all sites' list above the spaceport cards.
why: Read the page in full: only a grid of site cards built from getSiteSummaries(); no cross-site chronological launch list.

title: Rocket detail pages have zero photos of the rocket
evidence: curl of /rockets/falcon-9 - grep for `<img` returns exactly 1 match, the SpaceNexus logo; src/app/rockets/[slug]/page.tsx has no next/image usage for rocket imagery
experience: The Falcon 9 page has real substance but reads as a dense stat sheet - no hero shot, no pad photo - on a site whose audience is people who like rockets.
recommendation: Add a hero image per rocket at the top of every /rockets/[slug] page.
why: Only image hit in the [slug] template is the OG meta URL, never rendered. src/app/rockets/page.tsx (index) does use HeroArt, so the pattern exists but was never applied to the detail template.

title: The 'never miss a launch' alert hook - the actual retention mechanism - only appears on one page
evidence: src/components/ui/AlertNudge.tsx; `grep -rln AlertNudge src/app --include=page.tsx` returns only src/app/mission-control/page.tsx
experience: The natural moment to ask 'want us to remind you about this launch' is right after someone reads a rocket's next-launch date or a city viewing guide, but the prompt only lives inside the Mission Control mega-page.
recommendation: Surface a lightweight AlertNudge on rocket pages and viewing guides, scoped to that rocket's/site's next launch.
why: Confirmed by grep. AlertNudge's props are generic and reusable. Lines up with ROADMAP_2026-09.md Tier 2 #12.

title: Newsletter/subscribe is asked up to three times in one short session
evidence: src/app/page.tsx:486 (NewsletterSignup); src/app/mission-control/page.tsx:1771 (NewsletterSignup); global ExitIntentPopup (layout.tsx:338)
experience: In the home -> Mission Control loop a visitor can be asked for their email three times within minutes, none of the three aware the others just asked.
recommendation: Suppress the exit-intent popup once a signup module has already been shown/dismissed in the same session, using the existing dismissal keys.
why: 'newsletter-subscribed' is only read/written inside ExitIntentPopup.tsx (44,162); NewsletterSignup.tsx has zero storage calls. No cross-suppression exists.

title: Leftover dead files sit inside the folder for the site's single most important page
evidence: src/app/mission-control/page.tsx.bak and src/app/mission-control/_edit.js exist alongside the live page.tsx
experience: No direct visitor impact, but raises the odds of an editor picking up the wrong file as the page keeps growing.
recommendation: Delete page.tsx.bak and _edit.js; split the page's tab content into separate components.
why: ls confirms both files sit alongside the live page.tsx.

title: The flagship 'Markets' destination - Space Stocks - shows zero public companies in every category
evidence: Live /space-stocks header reads '0 public space companies, live'; all three category sections read 'No companies matched this category yet.' src/app/space-stocks/page.tsx:184-192 wraps the Prisma roster/IPO-class queries in try/catch and on any failure silently falls back to empty arrays with no user-visible error state. Space Stocks is the first, hot-flagged item in the Markets nav (site-directory.ts:86).
experience: A BD lead or analyst clicks Markets -> Space Stocks and sees a professional-looking page with nothing in it. Nothing tells them this is a bug rather than 'no public space companies exist yet.'
recommendation: Render a distinct 'data temporarily unavailable' state instead of an empty-but-valid-looking grid; page an owner on repeated failures; root-cause why getRoster()/getIpoClass() throw in production when the same fields render fine on individual company-profile pages.
why: Live-verified 2026-08-29. The query itself is well-formed against the current Prisma schema, so this is a live runtime failure being masked, not a code logic bug already fixed.

title: SpaceX's headline IPO valuation is reported as three different numbers across three pages
evidence: /company-profiles/spacex 'Valuation $1.8T' / 'Market Cap $1.9T'; /funding-tracker '$75.0B @ $1780.0B'; /space-stocks banner '~$2T market cap'
experience: An investor cross-checking a headline number finds the site disagreeing with itself on the biggest number in the industry.
recommendation: Derive valuation/market cap from one canonical field everywhere; label Valuation vs Market Cap distinctly.
why: Partially refuted. valuation=$1.78T and marketCap=$1.865T are two legitimately different fields, and funding-tracker's postValuation matches company.valuation exactly. The real bug is narrower: space-stocks' banner hardcodes literal text '~$2T' (page.tsx:245) sourced from no DB field. One stale marketing sentence plus a labeling gap, not a three-way data-integrity failure.

title: The industry's largest government contractor shows zero contracts and zero funding rounds
evidence: /company-profiles/lockheed-martin renders 'Government Contracts: 0' (page.tsx:911) and 'Funding History: 0' (line 650)
experience: A BD lead landing on the page to see what this company has been awarded gets a hard zero, on the company where the answer should be richest.
recommendation: Backfill GovernmentContract/FundingRound rows for the primes (Lockheed, Boeing, Northrop, L3Harris) from SAM.gov awards and SEC filings.
why: Live API confirms contracts: [], fundingRounds: [], acquisitions: [], partnerships: []. Same pattern on Boeing and Northrop Grumman (both totalFunding: 0).

title: Two unreconciled, unlabeled scoring systems shown on the same company page
evidence: src/app/company-profiles/[slug]/page.tsx:533-543 renders 'SpaceNexus Score' (Lockheed = 49, Grade D) directly above a section the code comments '// Legacy Scores' but the UI labels 'Detailed Intelligence Scores' (line 539), showing 92 Overall / 97 Market Position for the same company
experience: An analyst sees 49/D next to 92/97 for the identical company with no way to know which one the site stands behind.
recommendation: Remove the legacy CompanyScore rendering, or visibly label it 'Legacy scoring model (pre-2026), superseded by SpaceNexus Score above.'
why: Source-confirmed: the 'legacy' framing exists only in a code comment and never reaches the page.

title: Investor deal-count leaderboard double-counts the same firm under two names
evidence: /funding-tracker 'Top Investors by Deal Count': 'a16z (Andreessen Horowitz)' #3 and 'a16z' #8 are the same firm
experience: The exact question the widget exists to answer comes out wrong.
recommendation: Normalize investor name at write-time or add an alias/canonical-name table before aggregation.
why: Live API shows a THREE-way split: 'a16z (Andreessen Horowitz)' 10 deals, 'a16z' 7 deals, 'Andreessen Horowitz' 4 deals = 21, which would surpass Lux Capital's 19 for #1. stats/route.ts groups by exact string match with no normalization.

title: Markets nav's legacy /market route double-redirects into the broken Space Stocks page
evidence: src/app/market/page.tsx redirect('/market-intel'); next.config.js:486 /market-intel -> /space-stocks permanent
experience: Anyone who bookmarked the older URLs takes an extra hop only to land on the currently-broken page.
recommendation: Collapse to a single redirect straight to /space-stocks.
why: Worse than described: curl of /market returns HTTP 200 with a client-side meta-refresh ('1;url=/market-intel'), so a real visitor sees a 1-second flash of the wrong page before the chain completes.

title: The Relationships/Competitors tab renders completely blank instead of an empty state
evidence: src/app/company-profiles/[slug]/page.tsx:1845-1912 RelationshipsTab gates each section on `.length > 0` with no fallback branch
experience: A user who clicks 'Relationships' sees a tab that looks broken rather than honestly empty - inconsistent with the Financials and Contracts tabs on the same page.
recommendation: Add the same 'No X recorded' empty-state pattern used elsewhere; consider merging the curated competitor list and the auto-generated Similar Companies widget.
why: Source-confirmed; Lockheed's live data has all three arrays empty.

title: Stray literal '0' rendered on company cards with exactly-zero tracked funding
evidence: src/components/company/SimilarCompanies.tsx:166: `{company.totalFunding && company.totalFunding > 0 && (...)}` - when totalFunding is 0 React renders the literal 0
experience: Boeing and Northrop Grumman display as 'Defense0' on Lockheed's Similar Companies list.
recommendation: Change the guard to `Boolean(company.totalFunding) && ...`.
why: Source-confirmed; /similar returns Boeing and Northrop with totalFunding: 0.

title: No price history, chart, or range on any real stock surface - spot price only
evidence: SpaceStocksTables.tsx PriceCell/ChangeCell and company-profile Financial Snapshot show only current price and day-over-day %; no sparkline, 52-week range, volume or moving average anywhere
experience: A Bloomberg-terminal-minded visitor expects at minimum a trend line and 52-week range next to a ticker; a bare price reads as a shallow feed.
recommendation: Add a sparkline (30/90 days) and 52-week high/low to both surfaces, sourced from the quote API already in use.
why: No 'sparkline', '52-week', 'chart' or 'historical' references anywhere in either component.

title: Company financial data is often a single stale annual data point with no trend
evidence: /company-profiles/lockheed-martin 'Revenue Estimates' has exactly one row: '2024 | $67.6B | estimate | SEC Filing' against a current site date of August 2026
experience: An investor gauging trajectory gets one number frozen almost two years in the past.
recommendation: Backfill 2-3 years of annual revenue for public companies from 10-K filings and render as a trend row/sparkline.
why: Live API confirms exactly one revenueEstimates entry.

title: SpaceX's IPO is stated as settled historical fact with no editorial/speculative framing
evidence: /space-stocks 'POST-IPO WAVE' banner states flatly that SpaceX went public in June 2026 at ~$2T, with no sourcing note, while the Industry Benchmarks section directly below carries an explicit 'curated editorial benchmarks, not live-market data' disclosure
experience: A visitor cannot tell whether the most consequential financial claim on the page is verified live-market fact or a curated entry.
recommendation: Give the IPO-wave banner and 'Largest Funding Rounds' the same DataAsOf-style sourcing disclosure, with the source link surfaced.
why: Worse than described: the IpoRow type carries `sourceUrl` and `notes` fields (SpaceStocksTables.tsx:21-22) that are populated in the data layer but never rendered - the citation is literally dead code.

title: The persistent top-nav 'Jobs' link never reaches the job board
evidence: src/components/Navigation.tsx:460-465 (desktop) and :692-698 (mobile) hardcode href=/space-talent, outside the site-directory system. space-talent/page.tsx:1201-1202 defaults to the 'talent' tab. The real listings live under 'workforce', reached via next.config.js:372 or site-directory.ts:108.
experience: A visitor clicks Jobs in the nav on every page expecting ~6,500 ATS listings and lands on Talent & Experts, with the actual job board one unlabeled tab click away.
recommendation: Point both hardcoded top-nav Jobs links at /jobs so they match the Business-menu entry and the homepage persona CTA.
why: Verified all four file:line references directly.

title: 31-page Engineering & Operations group has no menu path at all
evidence: src/lib/site-directory.ts:150-185 - the 'ops' group's 31 entries have no menu:true, so Navigation.tsx's ALL_CATEGORIES never builds a dropdown. Two entries are hot:true (Launch Cost Calculator :153, Mission Simulator :154). No standalone /tools link exists in Navigation.tsx or Footer.tsx.
experience: Link budget, thermal, radiation, propulsion database, Mars planner and 24 more engineering references - including two proven traffic winners - are invisible in every menu.
recommendation: Give 'ops' menu:true for a sixth dropdown, or promote its two hot entries into an existing menu with nav:true.
why: Navigation.tsx's CategoryKey type only lists five groups; 'ops' literally cannot produce a dropdown. Grepped Navigation.tsx, Footer.tsx and layout.tsx: no standalone /tools link exists anywhere except the five 'Everything in X' anchors.

title: /ignition ships at sitemap priority 1.0 but has zero internal links
evidence: src/app/sitemap.ts:65 sets /ignition priority 1.0; grepping site-directory.ts, Navigation.tsx, Footer.tsx and related-content lists turns up nothing
experience: A substantial NASA moon-base tracker topically adjacent to /artemis that a visitor can never click their way to.
recommendation: Add it to site-directory.ts under 'launches' cross-linked from Artemis Tracker, or fold into /artemis and redirect.
why: Not re-verified in the verification pass; verify link-absence and traffic before acting.

title: An 8-page orphaned SaaS-marketing funnel draws crawl budget with no path back into the site
evidence: src/app/{why-spacenexus,business-models,customer-discovery,features,use-cases,alternatives,vs,solutions}/page.tsx appear in none of site-directory.ts, Navigation.tsx, Footer.tsx, but are listed in sitemap.ts
experience: A prospect landing from search has no link forward into the comparison, use-case or pricing content these pages feed.
recommendation: Wire the cluster into the site directory, or remove it in the next consolidation pass.
why: Overstated. Real inbound links verified for why-spacenexus, features, alternatives, business-models and customer-discovery. Only /use-cases and /vs have genuinely zero inbound links. The illustrative example is wrong: why-spacenexus/page.tsx:501-507 links out to /compare, /features, /pricing and /register.

title: Compliance Hub's Pro-gating is hardcoded in the nav but missing from the directory data model
evidence: src/app/compliance/page.tsx:594 PremiumGate requiredTier=pro; site-directory.ts:107 has no pro:true; Navigation.tsx hardcodes `item.href === '/compliance'` at :208 and :774; DirectoryBrowser.tsx:71 reads the generic e.pro field and shows no pill
experience: The same page is labeled PRO in the nav but shows no tier indicator on /tools.
recommendation: Set pro:true on the entry and delete the hardcoded href check.
why: Verified exactly as described at every cited line.

title: 'Compare' occupies a nav slot in two different dropdowns under two different labels
evidence: site-directory.ts:90 'Compare Companies' (Markets, nav:true) and :135 'Compare' (Learn, nav:true) - identical href /compare
experience: The same destination reads as two different things, and one of the smallest menus' scarce slots is spent twice.
recommendation: Keep nav:true in Markets only; free the Learn slot for something with no current menu presence.
why: Verified; both groups have exactly 6 nav:true entries.

title: Mobile menu's 'Show all N items' affordance is functionally dead weight
evidence: Navigation.tsx:785-806 shows the toggle only when items.length - MOBILE_INITIAL_ITEMS(8) > 0. Counts: Launches 9 (hidden=1), News 8, Markets 7, Business 7, Learn 7.
experience: A mobile user taps 'Show all 9 items' under Launches and gets one extra link; every other category never shows the control.
recommendation: Drop the show-more mechanism or raise MOBILE_INITIAL_ITEMS so it triggers meaningfully.
why: Arithmetic verified against current nav:true counts; MOBILE_INITIAL_ITEMS=8 at Navigation.tsx:32.

title: /space-tycoon/about 404s in production despite matching code on dev/origin/dev
evidence: curl -I returned 404; git shows dev in sync with origin/dev; sitemap.ts:306 lists it at priority 0.8
experience: A visitor or Googlebot hitting a sitemap-submitted URL gets 'Page Not Found'.
recommendation: Verify the live Railway deployment id matches the commit; force a redeploy if stuck.
why: Live-retested: /space-tycoon/about and /space-tycoon/dev-log both return 200 consistently across 6+ repeated curls. Local build manifest confirms both routes compile. The symptom was real at one instant but self-healed - consistent with a Railway rolling-deploy propagation window, not a standing defect. Supports the deploy-smoke-test finding rather than standing alone.

title: Homepage and /rockets are force-dynamic with zero CDN caching, unlike sibling pages
evidence: src/app/page.tsx:64 and src/app/rockets/page.tsx:8 export dynamic='force-dynamic'; curl -I shows 'private, no-cache, no-store' vs 's-maxage=31536000, stale-while-revalidate' on /mission-control and /news
experience: Every homepage visit re-runs a full DB query and SSR with no edge cache, adding latency and Railway compute cost that scales linearly with the 10k MAU push.
recommendation: Replace force-dynamic with `export const revalidate = 300` on the homepage and /rockets.
why: Verified both files and both live responses. Checked for cookies()/headers()/searchParams/session usage that would justify true dynamic rendering: none. The data is not user-specific.

title: /mission-control and /startups have no <h1> anywhere on the page
evidence: Rendered HTML H1_COUNT 0 for both; first heading is an <h2> at mission-control/page.tsx:586 and startups/page.tsx:229
experience: Two of the site's most important pages have no page-topic heading - screen readers get no landmark, search engines lose the strongest on-page signal after the title.
recommendation: Add a real <h1> above the first section on both pages.
why: Verified on live HTML and in source.

title: /startups renders a duplicated title suffix: '... | SpaceNexus | SpaceNexus'
evidence: src/app/startups/layout.tsx:4 sets the full suffixed title while root layout.tsx:96 template '%s | SpaceNexus' appends it again
experience: Browser tab and Google search result both show the broken double suffix.
recommendation: Drop the manual '| SpaceNexus' and let the root template supply it.
why: Verified live title string and both source lines.

title: No page-specific structured data on the site's main listing pages
evidence: Every fetched page carries the same 2 JSON-LD blocks from StructuredData.tsx; only space-stocks/page.tsx:199 adds an ItemList
experience: Search engines see identical generic organization markup instead of ItemList/FAQPage schema on the pages meant to draw search traffic.
recommendation: Add page-type schema: ItemList/Product for /rockets, ItemList for /launches, and for /mission-control, /tools, /chart.
why: 3 of 8 cited examples are false. /company-profiles already ships CollectionPage + ItemList + FAQPage + BreadcrumbList; /news already ships CollectionPage + ItemList; /guide/space-launch-cost-comparison already ships Article + FAQPage with 5 Q&A. The gap is real only for /rockets, /launches, /mission-control, /tools and /chart.

title: /space-stocks meta description is 310 characters, ~2x Google's display budget
evidence: Measured 306 chars from src/app/space-stocks/page.tsx:31 vs 125-201 on nine other pages; truncates mid-word at '...Lockhee'
experience: The value-proposition sentence gets cut off mid-word in the search snippet.
recommendation: Trim to one clear sentence under ~155 characters.
why: Measured at 306 chars; 'Lockheed' begins at character 193 so a ~200-char cutoff lands exactly at '...Lockhee'.

title: robots.txt blocks /widgets/ while sitemap.ts submits three specific widget URLs under that path
evidence: robots.txt 'Disallow: /widgets/'; sitemap.ts:446-448 lists /widgets/market-snapshot, /widgets/next-launch, /widgets/space-weather
experience: Search Console reports these as 'Submitted URL blocked by robots.txt'.
recommendation: Remove the three sub-pages from the sitemap, or remove the Disallow rule.
why: Verified live robots.txt and all four sitemap lines.

title: No deploy-freshness smoke test, so live 404s on shipped code go unnoticed
evidence: Two brand-new pages 404'd on first live check and returned 200 minutes later with no action taken
experience: Pages that pass local build and git sync can still serve broken responses in production before a human happens to click.
recommendation: Add a post-deploy job that curls a sample of sitemap URLs (weighted toward routes touched in recent commits) and alerts on non-200.
why: The cited commit evidence doesn't match this checkout's history, but the underlying pattern was independently reproduced. Impact reflects 'closes a narrow, self-healing propagation gap', not 'catches persistent broken deploys'.

title: Mission Debrief pages still show 'SCRUBBED' for six launches the site's own event data now marks 'completed'
evidence: Six /api/mission-debriefs slugs return status 'scrubbed' with fabricated narratives; the same eventIds return status 'completed' from /api/events for Aug 18-27
experience: A visitor sees a red SCRUBBED badge and an AI narrative about a scrub for a Starlink batch the site's own event record confirms flew. True for at least 6 debriefs spanning Aug 19-25.
recommendation: When the outcome-sync job flips an event's status, re-run or invalidate the mission-debrief generator for that eventId. Backfill the 6 identified debriefs now.
why: Verified live for falcon-9-block-5-starlink-group-15-20 (eventId cmsrt6mmv00rf13q8peedanp3). Root cause confirmed: src/app/api/cron/mission-debriefs/route.ts:110-117 bakes status from event.status once at creation and no job anywhere re-syncs an existing debrief.

title: Duplicate Mission Debrief pages for the same spacewalk with two different AI-written narratives
evidence: /api/mission-debriefs/us-eva-98 and /us-eva-98-2 - identical eventId cms3g0lqs463c3x6a5y4pwfji and missionDate, different executiveSummary
experience: Two live, separately-indexable URLs telling slightly different versions of the same spacewalk.
recommendation: Add a uniqueness constraint on eventId in the generator; 301-redirect us-eva-98-2 to us-eva-98.
why: Verified live; both return the same eventId and missionDate with differently-worded summaries.

title: Falcon 9's per-kg launch cost and list price are stated differently on at least 6 live pages
evidence: $2,700/kg in resources-data.ts:1213, tool-faqs.ts:16, SpaceQuiz.tsx:136, industry-trends/page.tsx:77, space-stocks/page.tsx:18; $2,940 and $2,900 in blog-content.ts:14981,:9931; $3,000 in cost-to-launch.ts:72,85; $3,070 in guide/space-launch-cost-comparison/page.tsx:16,35; rideshare $5,500 in space-manufacturing/page.tsx:243 vs $7,000 in cost-to-launch.ts:84. List price $67M vs $70M.
experience: A visitor reading /space-stocks sees ~$2,700/kg, clicks to the guide and sees $3,070/kg, then finds two different rideshare figures for the same thing.
recommendation: Create one constant (src/lib/launch-cost-constants.ts) for list price, dedicated $/kg and rideshare $/kg, dated with a source, and import it everywhere.
why: Verified every cited location in code.

title: Newsletter signup page shows a fake preview dated in March while advertising itself as 'Weekly'
evidence: src/app/newsletter/page.tsx:58 'Free Weekly Newsletter'; :254-280 hardcoded sample with 'Mar 19' and 'Mar 22' launch dates
experience: The page a visitor lands on to decide whether to subscribe calls the product 'Weekly' although it was renamed to the twice-weekly M/Th Digest on 8/24, and its sample shows five-month-old dates.
recommendation: Pull a real recent digest excerpt from /intelligence-brief at render time, or at minimum update the dates and correct 'Weekly' to 'Twice-weekly (Mon/Thu)'.
why: Verified stale copy and dates, but the mock is explicitly labeled 'Sample Issue Preview' with a 'Preview' pill, which softens the 'visitor thinks this is live' framing.

title: 'Chart of the Week' exists in code but is invisible outside /chart and the email digest
evidence: src/lib/charts/registry.ts chartOfTheWeekSlug(); no reference to it or /chart in page.tsx, LandingHero.tsx or mission-control
experience: A feature built to give repeat visitors a reason to come back weekly only surfaces to people who already know to visit /chart.
recommendation: Add a 'Chart of the Week' card to the homepage and/or Mission Control linking to /chart/[slug].
why: Confirmed by grep and live fetch. Context: Chart of the Week shipped 2026-08-29 and was deliberately scoped to a digest slot, so the narrow initial scope was intentional; the recommendation adds a link, not a surface.

title: Regulatory 'AI Insight' items are often content-free bureaucratic filler
evidence: /api/ai-insights: a 2026-08-29 item whose summary states 'the Federal Register did not publish an abstract describing the specific changes'; ~6 of the last 30 insights are templated BIS entity-list removals
experience: A visitor filtering by 'Regulatory' gets a wall of near-identical low-information items, diluting the strong forecast/market pieces on the same page.
recommendation: Suppress or batch-summarize regulatory items where the source publishes no abstract - roll several into one weekly 'Entity List changes' digest item.
why: Verified live; ~20% of the top-30 are this genre, close to the original 23% claim.

title: AI Insights feed has a ~4-month content gap (mid-March to mid-August) with no indication to the reader
evidence: /api/ai-insights?page=1&limit=30 jumps from 2026-08-12 to 2026-04-01 and 2026-03-14
experience: A visitor paging back hits a wall where the site apparently stopped producing analysis for four months, with no note explaining the pause.
recommendation: Add a visible note ('Insights paused Mar-Jul 2026, resumed Aug 2026') wherever the feed is browsed by date, consistent with /intelligence-brief.
why: Verified live; /intelligence-brief does carry an equivalent note and /ai-insights does not.

title: /news, /ai-insights and /intelligence-brief render nothing for any client that doesn't execute JS
evidence: curl returns ~108KB of shell with zero article strings; all content loads client-side per NewsPageClient.tsx:84, ai-insights/page.tsx:157, intelligence-brief/page.tsx:69
experience: The pages meant to earn return visits and rank for space-news queries show a crawler or slow-JS client a loading shell, not headlines or dates.
recommendation: Server-render the first page of results, hydrating client-side for filtering/pagination.
why: Verified via curl and source on all three.

title: Slip-history and debrief content types are strong but under-cross-linked
evidence: /chart includes a 'Launch date slips per week' chart; launch surfaces do not link to a specific debrief or to the slip chart
experience: A user reading about a specific launch has no link to that launch's own debrief once it has flown, and no link to the slip-history chart.
recommendation: Deep-link each flown launch to its /mission-debriefs/[slug]; add a 'see this provider's slip history' link.
why: Overstated: src/components/launches/LaunchCrossLinks.tsx already exists and is wired into launch/[eventId], launches/[site] and rockets/[slug]. The residual gap is real but narrower - the debriefs link goes to the generic index rather than the specific slug, and no slip-history link exists anywhere.

title: News feed source mix skews toward one aggregator
evidence: A snapshot showed SpaceDaily at 12/40 (30%) of the feed
experience: A repeat visitor checking /news daily notices a lot of same-sourced items rather than a spread of original reporting.
recommendation: Consider a source-diversity cap (~20% per source per day).
why: Re-checked live: SpaceDaily is 8/40 (20%), already at the finding's own proposed cap. A rotating RSS feed's single snapshot is not evidence of persistent skew, and today's snapshot contradicts it.

title: Mission Control renders every event in one unbounded DOM list - 30k-54k px of scroll
evidence: src/app/mission-control/page.tsx:1524-1567 (years.map > month.map > monthEvents.map, no slice/pagination/virtualization); events fetch passes limit:'500' at line 1206; measured 30,183px at 1440px and 53,785px at 390px
experience: A visitor opens Mission Control expecting a dashboard and gets a flat timeline of ~100 events, each a full EventCard. On a phone that is 53k+ pixels before the content sections that follow.
recommendation: Cap the initial render to the current + next month with 'Load more'/'Jump to month', and virtualize the rest.
why: Source and live measurement both verified; 53,785px reproduced exactly.

title: Carousel dot indicators are 8x8px (32x8px active) - far under any usable tap target
evidence: src/components/ModuleNavBar.tsx:206-211 and src/components/modules/ModuleContainer.tsx:394-399 - `w-2 h-2` inactive / `w-8 h-2` active, no padding; confirmed live via getBoundingClientRect
experience: The only way to jump to a specific module on a phone is tapping an 8px dot, so users mis-tap the neighbouring dot or the carousel arrow.
recommendation: Wrap each dot in a min-w-[44px] min-h-[44px] button with the dot centered, matching TrialCountdownBanner's existing fix.
why: Both files verified verbatim.

title: Two nearly-identical trial banners exist; only one got the 44px tap-target fix
evidence: src/components/TrialBanner.tsx:51-54 dismiss button has p-0.5 with no min-width/height (computed 20x20); src/components/billing/TrialCountdownBanner.tsx:152-155 has p-1.5 min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px]. Both mounted in layout.tsx:297 and :306.
experience: The same dismiss gesture is either an easy 44px tap or a fiddly 20px tap depending on which banner is showing.
recommendation: Delete TrialBanner.tsx or bring its dismiss button up to the same pattern; two components for one concept is worth consolidating.
why: Verified both files and both mount points.

title: At least five visually different 'primary CTA' button styles compete on the pages that matter most
evidence: globals.css:405-455 defines a documented 3-level button hierarchy. None of the landing CTAs use it: page.tsx:321 uses `rounded` + inline style background var(--accent-primary); HowItWorks.tsx:99 and DemoShowcase.tsx:392 use bg-white rounded-lg; LiveStreamSection.tsx:730 uses bg-white rounded-full; :156 uses bg-red-600 rounded-full.
experience: On the homepage a user sees four unrelated shapes/colors all claiming to be the primary action, none matching the class the rest of the app standardized on.
recommendation: Route every landing CTA through .btn-primary/.btn-secondary/.btn-ghost or a shared Button component.
why: Each cited line verified. 'Five' is a slight overcount (HowItWorks and DemoShowcase are the same style) but the substance holds.

title: Mobile full-screen nav menu has no focus trap, no Escape-to-close, and no aria-modal
evidence: src/components/Navigation.tsx:613-617 is a plain fixed inset-0 div with a click-backdrop; grep for 'Escape' finds only the desktop dropdown handler at :135. src/components/ui/OnboardingTour.tsx:202-235 implements all three for the same class of overlay.
experience: A keyboard user can Tab into the hamburger menu but has no Escape shortcut, and nothing stops Tab from moving focus into the dimmed content behind it.
recommendation: Reuse the focus-trap/Escape/aria-modal logic already written for OnboardingTour.
why: Verified: isMenuOpen has no keydown listener at all; OnboardingTour.tsx:205 and :256-257 do.

title: On a phone, four independent overlays can stack and one covers the page's own primary button
evidence: Screenshot at 390px on /space-tycoon/about: promo banner + Play Store banner + nav + breadcrumb + Quick Start checklist + cookie bar simultaneously
experience: A first-time mobile visitor sees five stacked chrome layers before reaching page content.
recommendation: Give the independently-mounted overlays a shared z-index/priority scheme so at most one non-essential overlay shows at a time.
why: Stacking is real (10+ simultaneous fixed elements measured), but the causal claim is wrong: elementFromPoint identifies the covering element as OnboardingTour's persona-picker modal (fixed inset-0 z-[9998]), not the cookie bar (z-[60]). That modal is role=dialog, aria-modal, Escape-dismissible and once-per-browser - a legitimate one-time gate, not an unintended overlay.

title: Site is dark-only with no light theme, and emoji icons are mixed with a custom SVG icon system
evidence: grep for prefers-color-scheme / data-theme in globals.css returns no matches; OnboardingTour.tsx:29-37 PERSONAS uses raw emoji while BentoFeatures.tsx and the nav use stroke SVG icons
experience: No light theme for an investor reading in a bright office; emoji render with a different art style per OS, breaking the line-icon visual language in the onboarding flow every new user sees first.
recommendation: Replace persona-picker/checklist emoji with the stroked-SVG icon set; treat a light theme as a longer-term backlog item.
why: Both claims verified in source. Impact 2 is appropriate given the finding frames itself as backlog.
